fields.why: The methods say WHO/UNICEF estimates 'are used throughout this report', but the limitations refer to coverage 'based on administrative data', so B's 'other' for Indonesia's administrative reports is defensible. Rule needed: a non-US country's national program or surveillance data count as international surveillance, not 'other'.

The article defines 'remote and high-risk areas' by population immunity, surveillance quality and vulnerable groups, not by rurality, so B's omission is slightly better; A's descriptor-only rurality is defensible and does not change the level (1).

A records pandemic service disruptions (closed posts, movement restrictions, staff repurposing) offered to explain a decline over time, not social or structural determinants of any group difference. Rule needed: record determinants only when they are offered as social/structural explanations, not as health-service disruptions behind a trend.

brief_issues: Unclear whether a non-US national program's administrative data are 'international surveillance' or 'other', and whether pandemic service disruptions (incl. movement restrictions) count as structural/political determinants when no disparity is analyzed.
